Well-Being Ring / Well-Being Design Series / Episode 02

Beyond the Surface.

Stress apps and wearables already show you things. They still leave the next move to you.

I compared what each product does for stress with what it leaves open. The gap is in the experience, not the sensor.

How I checked: I read each company's own pages through web searches in November 2026. This is not a full audit, so I describe what each product is designed to do.

01  What each one does

Four groups, one pattern.

Calm and Headspace

What it does

Lots of calming audio: meditations, sleep stories and breathing exercises.

What it leaves open

You pick from many options when you are already stressed. It does not use your body data to choose for you.

Fitbit and Pixel Watch

What it does

Tracks your heart rate, heart-rate variability and skin temperature. It gives you a stress score and a health coach.

What it leaves open

When it spots stress, it asks you to think about your mood and what caused it. It does not give you one step to take, and I did not find a way to check if it helped.

Oura

What it does

Shows your stress during the day, and has an AI advisor you can ask questions.

What it leaves open

You get scores, trends and advice, but you still work out what they mean and what to do. I did not find a way to check if it helped.

Ultrahuman

What it does

Sends small reminders through the day, such as when to stop having caffeine.

What it leaves open

The reminders are general, not about your stress right now. I did not find a counselor, doctor or emergency option.

02  Side by side

What changes next.

Well-Being Ring uses the same kind of ring sensing. The difference is what happens after the signal.

ProductMain approachHow Well-Being Ring is different

Calm and Headspace

Large libraries of audio. The user picks what to play.

Well-Being Ring gives one guided action, chosen from live body signals.

Fitbit and Pixel Watch

Stress scores, trends and a health coach.

Well-Being Ring turns the signal into one guided step, and is designed to show whether it helped.

Oura

Daytime stress and an AI advisor, with scores and advice.

Well-Being Ring is designed to guide you in the moment, with breathing that follows your heart rate.

Ultrahuman

General coaching nudges through the day.

Well-Being Ring has a built-in path from AI chat to a counselor, a doctor and emergency help.

03  The pattern

Every product asks for energy at the worst moment.

Each one needs the person to browse, read or interpret, when they have the least energy for it.

04  Where the gap is

The gap is in the experience, not the sensor.

Oura and Ultrahuman already measure stress with rings, so sensing is not the gap. In the products above, I did not find any of these:

  1. 01

    One clear action, not a menu

  2. 02

    Breathing that follows live heart rate

  3. 03

    A before-and-after result that shows whether it worked

  4. 04

    One path from AI chat to counselor, doctor and emergency help

  5. 05

    Consent-based sharing of a stress summary with a counselor or doctor

  6. 06

    A trusted-person alert if stress stays critical

Well-Being Ring's answer: one clear action, adapted to live heart rate, with a check that it worked, and a human path when it is not enough. The app is designed to do this.

05  Limits

It senses the body, not feelings.

Rings like these detect physical signs of activation, not emotions. They are not medical devices. Well-Being Ring is designed to support wellbeing, and it does not diagnose.
